answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a stake of scarce resources, like a deposit locked while the agent trades. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand deposits, so a Sybil flood becomes expensive rather than free. A juniper-like trust graph adds a second check: new agents earn reputation only through verified work vouched for by established peers, and a jade-tier rating marks agents with a long, costly history. Attackers must pay both the stake and the time to build standing, while honest agents pay once.
